intro: Traditions disagree about what exists at the most fundamental level and about the status of the everyday world. The rows summarise each position in its own terms.

rows.claim: Only Brahman is ultimately real; the world is appearance (maya).
rows.detail: The world is real for practical purposes but, from the ultimate standpoint, is an appearance of Brahman, neither real nor unreal. Brahman is pure existence-consciousness-bliss.

rows.claim: Brahman is real, qualified by real selves and a real world.
rows.detail: Selves and matter are real and inseparable from Brahman, as a body is from its soul. The world is a real transformation of Brahman's body.

rows.claim: God, souls and matter are all real and really distinct.
rows.detail: God alone is independent; souls and matter are real but dependent. Five kinds of difference are real and eternal.

rows.claim: Two eternal principles: conscious purushas and unconscious prakriti.
rows.detail: The world is the real evolution of prakriti into twenty-three principles through the interplay of the three gunas. Purusha does not change.

rows.claim: A plurality of real categories: substances, qualities, actions, universals and more.
rows.detail: Physical things are built from eternal atoms; selves, minds, space and time are also substances. Wholes, universals and relations are real.

rows.claim: No permanent substances; schools differ on what is ultimately real.
rows.detail: Abhidharma schools treat momentary elements (dharmas) as ultimate; Madhyamaka holds all things empty of intrinsic nature; Yogacara holds experience is structured by consciousness.

rows.claim: Six real substances; reality is many-sided, permanent and changing.
rows.detail: Souls, matter, space, time and the media of motion and rest are real. Anekantavada holds that any single standpoint captures only part of reality.

rows.claim: Only Shiva-consciousness is real, and the world is its real expression.
rows.detail: The world is not illusory but consciousness freely manifesting itself through thirty-six tattvas.

rows.claim: Only the perceptible material world is real.
rows.detail: As reported, only the four elements and their combinations exist; there is no unseen reality beyond them.

note: The central issues are whether reality is ultimately one or many, whether the everyday world is fully real, and whether consciousness or matter is fundamental.
